sources.title: How ABB and Econowind optimize the route to wind-assisted shipping

scope.technology: Econowind VentoFoil suction-based wing system with ABB SPOS routing
scope.commercial_deployment: 2025 contract for approximately 150 VentoFoil units across 50 vessels
scope.routing_platform_adoption: ABB Ability SPOS reported adopted on more than 4,500 vessels
scope.operating_method: weather and route optimization by the ship's Master using routing tools

observations.statement: ABB reports VentoFoil can help maintain required transit speed on lower main-engine power, with claimed fuel reductions of 6-10%.
ABB reports a 2025 Econowind contract covering about 150 VentoFoil units for 50 vessels.
ABB reports SPOS has been adopted on more than 4,500 vessels.

limitations: Vendor partnership publication; claimed fuel-savings range is not presented as an independent controlled trial result.
The 150 units/50 vessels is a supply-contract figure, not evidence that every unit is already installed or operating.
The 4,500-vessel SPOS adoption count is not the number of VentoFoil vessels.
Weather routing, VentoFoil and other vessel upgrades interact; their effects require a matched counterfactual.
Do not transfer 6-10% to a deep-sea cargo vessel without route, device count, apparent-wind and service matching.
eligible_use: Vendor claims benchmark with attribution preserved
ineligible_use: Independent proof of net vessel fuel saving
VentoFoil installed-fleet count inferred from SPOS

observations.statement: BAR lists average fuel saving of 1.5 tonnes/day for the 37.5m variant.

BAR lists average fuel saving of 0.7 tonnes/day for the 20-24m variant.
BAR lists achievable fuel saving of 0.9 tonnes/day for the 20-24m variant.

limitations: Product-page figures are vendor claims; detailed route/weather, vessel baseline, statistical variation and uncertainty are not supplied on this page.
Daily tonnes are not a transferable percentage and depend on baseline fuel consumption and operating conditions.
WindWings has specific folding/deck-space integration and structural requirements.
Compare net main-engine fuel after auxiliaries, route, installation mass/volume, cargo access, pilotage and availability.

ineligible_use: Direct numerical comparison to rotor/suction devices without matched route and vessel

sources.title: Integrated Design and Dynamic Performance Optimisation of Hybrid Electric Propulsion Systems for Coastal Cargo Vessels Under Real-World Operational Profiles

scope.candidate: diesel generator sets, DC bus, propulsion motors and lithium-ion battery storage
scope.design_method: bi-level sizing optimization with dynamic-programming energy management and battery degradation-aware lifecycle cost

observations.statement: The article reports 16-21% fuel savings for its optimized hybrid configuration relative to its mechanical baseline.
The article reports 17-20% CO2 reduction relative to its mechanical baseline.
The article reports 8-14% lifecycle cost reduction relative to its mechanical baseline.
The optimized case reports 2.3 MW installed generator power compared with 6.0 MW in its mechanical baseline.
The optimized case reports a 1.6 MWh battery energy storage system.

limitations: This is a specific coastal cargo case, not a deep-sea container-ship result.
The article uses reconstructed AIS/logbook operating profiles and a model-based optimization; it is not an independent sea-trial measurement of the claimed savings.
The authors identify simplified resistance/propulsion modeling and incomplete representation of fouling, extreme weather and manoeuvring.
The lower-level offline dynamic-programming controller assumes perfect knowledge of future voyage power profiles.
Do not transfer percentages, installed power or battery size to another route/vessel.
eligible_use: Baseline for a coastal-vessel branch of the programme

hybrid_design_space.architecture: DC bus, diesel generator sets, propulsion motors and lithium-ion ESS

operational_profile.data_gap_repair: For gaps longer than 15 minutes, linear interpolation or speed extrapolation is used.
operational_profile.source_data_availability: Data and code available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request; not a public raw-data download.

degradation_sensitivity.description: The article reports fuel-reduction/battery-lifetime trade-offs for different degradation weightings.

methodological_details: The lower-level dynamic-programming energy-management policy assumes perfect knowledge of each voyage's future power profile; this is an offline design upper bound, not a deployable online controller.
The propulsion-power reconstruction uses simplified resistance and propulsion relations and assumes a single-screw arrangement; higher-order hull-propeller-rudder interaction effects are neglected.
The article identifies incomplete representation of hull fouling, extreme weather and detailed manoeuvring.

Battery ageing uses laboratory-derived cycle-life data represented as a stationary cycle-life surface with pack-level scaling assumptions; thermal gradients and cell-to-cell variation are not fully represented.
Long AIS data gaps are repaired by interpolation or speed extrapolation; the effects of that repair policy should be stress-tested.
Five statistically representative typical operating profiles are used for the optimization, rather than scoring every voyage as a held-out observation.

sources.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning with Monotonic Constraints for Daily Fuel Consumption and CII Prediction of Ships
sources.publisher: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering

vessels: Poseidon large cruise ship, diesel-electric, 12 months, 12430 rows
Triton small cruise ship, direct-drive diesel, 3 months, 9575 rows
Ceto offshore support vessel, thruster pods, 6 months, 7102 rows
method: partial monotonic constraints for Random Forest and XGBoost
five rotated time folds and split-consistent OOF

limitations: Empirical measured-data study covers two cruise ships and one offshore support vessel, not mainstream cargo vessels.
FuelCast target is total daily onboard fuel, not propulsion-only or shaft fuel.
FuelCast records omit trim and do not represent large cargo loading/draft cycles.
Wind-assisted ship physics requires conditional constraints; global wind-speed monotonicity is not valid when favourable wind/device state may reduce engine demand.
Reported values are author-reported and require independent reproduction.

Public daily measured-data software pipeline test, subject to dataset license

scope.vessel_class: Northern European short-sea cargo liner vessels
scope.retrofit_devices: Three Norsepower Rotor Sails per vessel

observations.attribution: Sea-Cargo own figures as quoted by Norsepower
observations.statement: The announcement attributes up to 35% lower CO2 emissions per tonne transported to the comprehensive rebuild programme.

observations.attribution: Sea-Cargo own figures as quoted by Norsepower
observations.statement: The announcement reports up to 50% total emissions reduction across the upgraded fleet.
Norsepower states the rotor sails can generate thrust equivalent to approximately 7,500 kW under favourable wind conditions.
Norsepower states mechanical installation took as little as two working days per vessel.

limitations: Vendor press release containing operator self-reported figures, not an independently audited performance dataset.
The CO2 reductions apply to a comprehensive retrofit including rotors, solar, batteries, power management and optimized propulsion; do not attribute the full figure to rotor sails alone.
The 7,500 kW figure is favourable-condition equivalent thrust, not annual average delivered propulsion power or a fuel-saving percentage.
No underlying voyage traces, counterfactual weather correction, uncertainty intervals or raw emissions accounting are supplied in the announcement.
Short-sea fixed liner operation is not a substitute for deep-sea container/bulk route validation.

ineligible_use: Independent proof of 35% rotor-only CO2 reduction
